messages.content: Solve word problems step by step.
Train A leaves city X at 60 km/h heading east. Train B leaves city Y (300 km east) at 80 km/h heading west, 30 minutes later. When and where do they meet?

message.content:
<think>We need to solve a relative motion problem. Train A leaves city X at 60 km/h heading east. Train B leaves city Y at 80 km/h heading west, 30 minutes later. City Y is 300 km east of city X. So the distance between X and Y is 300 km. Train A heads east, so from X towards Y. Train B heads west, so from Y towards X. They are moving towards each other. Train A leaves earlier (by 30 minutes). We need to find when (time after Train A leaves? Or after Train B leaves?) and where (distance from X) they meet.

We can set up equations.

Let t = time after Train A leaves (in hours). Then Train A distance traveled = 60 t km.

Train B leaves 0.5 h later, so its travel time = t - 0.5 (if t >= 0.5). Its speed = 80 km/h, so distance traveled = 80 (t - 0.5) km.

The sum of distances traveled equals the initial separation: 60 t + 80 (t - 0.5) = 300 km.

Solve: 60t + 80t - 40 = 300 => 140t = 340 => t = 340/140 = 34/14 = 17/7 ≈ 2.428571... hours.

Thus they meet at t = 2.428571... hours after Train A left. That is 2 hours + 0.428571*60 = 2 hours + 25.714 minutes ≈ 2 hours 25 minutes 42.86 seconds.

Alternatively, we can compute meeting point distance from X: distance = 60 t = 60 * 17/7 = (60*17)/7 = 1020/7 ≈ 145.7142857 km east of X.

Alternatively, distance from Y: 300 - distance from X = 154.2857 km.

Check: Train B traveled 80 (t - 0.5) = 80 * (17/7 - 0.5) = 80 * (17/7 - 1/2) = 80 * ((34 - 7)/14) = 80 * (27/14) = (80*27)/14 = (2160)/14 = 1080/7 ≈ 154.2857 km. Yes.
